words.definition_en: idiom: to immediately like and get along with someone
example_sentences: We hit it off right from the first conversation.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to gradually stop being close to someone
example_sentences: They grew apart after moving to different cities.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to slowly become less close to someone over time
example_sentences: Old friends sometimes drift apart after school.

words.definition_en: to continue feeling angry about something someone did
example_sentences: He still holds a grudge against his old boss.

words.translation_pt: fazer as pazes, enterrar o machado de guerra
words.definition_en: idiom: to end a conflict and become friendly again
example_sentences: The brothers finally buried the hatchet after years of silence.

words.definition_en: to tell someone a secret because you trust them
example_sentences: She confides in her best friend about everything.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to start talking honestly about personal feelings
example_sentences: It took him a while to open up to her.

words.definition_en: too emotionally dependent on another person
example_sentences: He can be a bit clingy in relationships.

words.definition_en: a promise or dedication to something, such as a relationship
example_sentences: He wasn't ready for that kind of commitment.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to start living a stable life, often with a partner
example_sentences: She wants to settle down and have kids.

words.definition_en: to formally ask someone to marry you
example_sentences: He proposed to her on the beach.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to end a romantic relationship
example_sentences: They broke up after two years together.

words.definition_en: to resume a romantic relationship after separating
example_sentences: They got back together after a month apart.

words.definition_en: a person perfectly suited to you
example_sentences: She believes he's her soulmate.

words.definition_en: no longer close to someone, especially a family member
example_sentences: He's been estranged from his father for years.

words.definition_en: idiom: a family member seen as different or disgraced
example_sentences: He's always been the black sheep of the family.

words.definition_en: unfair preference for one person over others
example_sentences: She accused her parents of favouritism.

words.definition_en: competition or jealousy between brothers and sisters
example_sentences: Sibling rivalry is common in large families.

words.definition_en: to show excessive love and attention to someone
example_sentences: Grandparents tend to dote on their grandchildren.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to resemble an older family member
example_sentences: She takes after her mother.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to admire and respect someone
example_sentences: I've always looked up to my older brother.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to have a friendly relationship with someone
example_sentences: I get along well with my neighbours.

words.definition_en: insincere; saying different things to different people
example_sentences: He's two-faced — nice to your face, but not behind your back.

words.definition_en: to betray someone who trusted you
example_sentences: She felt backstabbed by her closest friend.

words.definition_en: unreliable, especially about keeping plans or promises
example_sentences: He's so flaky — he always cancels last minute.

words.translation_pt: deixar plantado, faltar a um encontro
words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to fail to meet someone as arranged
example_sentences: He stood her up on their first date.

words.definition_en: collocation: an uncomfortable pause in conversation
example_sentences: There was an awkward silence after his joke.

words.definition_en: light, informal conversation about unimportant topics
example_sentences: He's not a big fan of small talk.

words.definition_en: idiom: to do something to make people feel more relaxed
example_sentences: He told a joke to break the ice.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to spend time relaxing socially with others
example_sentences: We usually hang out on weekends.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to talk with someone you haven't seen for a while
example_sentences: Let's meet for coffee and catch up.

words.definition_en: (of a group) closely bonded and supportive
example_sentences: They come from a close-knit community.

words.definition_en: a person who prefers quiet, solitary activities
example_sentences: As an introvert, she finds big parties tiring.

words.definition_en: a person who enjoys being with other people
example_sentences: He's a real extrovert — he loves meeting new people.

words.definition_en: friendly and confident in social situations
example_sentences: She's very outgoing and makes friends easily.

words.definition_en: slow to reveal emotions or opinions
example_sentences: He's quite reserved when you first meet him.
